title: Content: routine & block library (SPEC §7)
description: Curated personal workout content on top of the data-driven schema: the canonical W1-W4 routines, stable movement identities, private form-focused clip packs, and later physio content after the real-phone gate. Content files appear in the picker without app-code changes. WorkoutX GIFs are only a low-priority built-in fallback; private sources and derived clips remain outside the public repository.
acceptance_criteria: All shipped routines validate and appear with zero app-code changes; every visual-required W1-W4 movement resolves to a private silent loop/poster, an explicitly reused reference-v1 asset, or a deliberate poster/text-only classification; physio content remains hard-gated and cited; all non-deferred children close.

title: GIF fetch script + committed quota ledger (SPEC §6.10)
description:
node scripts/fetch-gifs.mjs <exerciseId...> (SPEC §6.10, §4): reads WORKOUTX_KEY from env (never committed — public repo), downloads missing GIFs to data/gifs/, skips files already present, paces under 30 req/min, records the X-Quota-Remaining response header, and appends {date, ids, calls, quotaRemaining} to a committed ledger (data/quota-ledger.json). Treat 503 'watermarked GIF unavailable' (known: ids 5202, 5204) as skip-and-report so a substitute can be chosen — never retry a 503 into the quota. ~330 of 500 monthly calls remain as of 2026-08-10; batch fetches per design session.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Running twice for the same ids costs zero API calls the second time.
- Ledger matches the API's reported quota drift.
- A 503 id is skipped with a clear report and no retries.
acceptance_criteria: second run for same ids costs zero calls; ledger matches API quota drift; 503 ids skip with report, no retry
notes: The approved useful-first visual path is now the private clip-pack graph. Keep this quota-aware WorkoutX GIF fetcher for future catalog gaps only; it is no longer the next delivery priority.

title: Produce the W1-W4 private clip pack (w1w4-v1)
description: Run the generic private clip pipeline over the validated W1-W4 v2 source map to produce the w1w4-v1 pack in the retained private media workspace. Reuse reference-v1 assets by stable movementId where they are an honest variant match. For remaining movements, cut silent loops and posters from the retained 16-video corpus first; download another source only for a proven gap. Normal movements should show roughly 2–5 clean complete reps (usually 5–10 seconds), with phase-matched seams. Holds and slow mobility use an intentionally useful judged duration. Apply explicit per-clip crops to keep the trainer at a consistent useful scale while preserving hands, feet, equipment and the full motion path. No source or derived media enters Git.
acceptance_criteria: Pack validation proves every W1-W4 visual-required movementId resolves to a w1w4-v1 16:9 landscape loop+poster, an honest reference-v1 reuse, or a deliberate poster/text-only classification; loops/crops pass normal and half-speed visual review with consistent prominent subject scale and full motion-path margins; ffprobe proves zero audio streams; manifests include dimensions, duration, hashes, framing and provenance; re-runs are idempotent; Git remains media-clean.

title: Implement four integrated routines (v2) as app data — W1-W4 super workouts
description:
## Background
docs/research/draft-routines-v2.md is the canonical, already-reviewed definition of four personal workouts: Iron Roots and Silk Coils at 30 minutes, Dragon Longform and Crane Longform at 45 minutes. This bead turns that specification into runnable app data. Visual clip discovery is deliberately downstream; routine semantics must not wait for perfect media.

## Technical Approach
Implement all four routines against schemaVersion 2 and stable movementId values. Preserve every interval, side, tempo, RPE, regression and global safety cue from the v2 document. Reuse blocks only where it removes real duplication. Register all routines through data/content-index.json with zero application-code changes. Keep the final 20-second rest so durations are exactly 30:00 or 45:00. Resolve visuals through the built-in media-pack fallback: an absent private clip is allowed to use an existing GIF, poster or deliberate text card. Do not fetch new WorkoutX GIFs as part of this bead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- W1-W4 exactly match the v2 interval counts, ordering, sides and coaching rules.
- Each routine validates against schemaVersion 2, appears in the picker without app-code changes, and runs end-to-end for exactly 30:00 or 45:00.
- Every interval has a stable movementId and a valid built-in visual or deliberate text fallback.
- The unique movement list can be consumed mechanically by the later form-focused clip-source bead.

## Test Plan
Run the schema validator over all four routines, unit tests, PWA checks, and a browser accelerated end-to-end pass for each routine including the final rest and completion state.

## Considerations
This bead owns routine data, not video search, downloading, clip production or player code.
acceptance_criteria: W1-W4 match v2 exactly, validate on schema v2, appear with zero app-code changes, run for exact durations, and expose stable movement IDs with safe built-in fallbacks.

title: Slice MadFit 07c6wlJh89U into the first 30-exercise private clip pack
description:
## Background
MadFit video 07c6wlJh89U is the exact source for the existing 30-interval workout. This bead builds the first real private clip database from that one video before broader channel search.

## Technical Approach
Use the generic clip-production pipeline and a private source download at no more than 720p. For every interval displayName in data/blocks/madfit-30min-hiit.json, record the exact 40-second work window and choose a clean 1-3-repetition loop, normally 3-8 seconds. Produce one no-audio loop and poster for each of the 30 named intervals, with distinct side records and complete compound sequences. The private reference-v1 catalogue records stable movementId, exact current displayName, video ID/URL, timestamps and loop range, side, equipment, viewpoint, framing/mirroring, form and seam notes, prospective mocap range, duration, dimensions, size and hash.

## Acceptance Criteria
- reference-v1 contains exactly one correctly named usable loop and poster for all 30 current MadFit interval names.
- Every loop shows a complete repetition/compound sequence with correct side/equipment and no obvious crop, long hold or broken seam.
- ffprobe reports zero audio streams and pack validation reports complete unique coverage.
- The catalogue contains enough timing/framing/form metadata for later wireframe mocap.
- Intervals 2, 16, 19 and 27 are visibly more informative than their current text/weak GIF fallback.
- Source and derived media stay outside Git; re-running does not redownload or re-encode completed work.

## Test Plan
Validate exact coverage against the current block JSON, run the pipeline's ffprobe/hash audit, and manually review every loop at normal and half speed. Import/offline phone behavior is owned by ft-mvp-ow6.15.

## Considerations
This bead uses only video 07c6wlJh89U. Cross-channel gap filling is ft-content-e0q.8.
acceptance_criteria: All 30 MadFit interval names have correctly mapped private silent 16:9 landscape loops/posters. Normal loops show roughly 2–5 complete reps with clean phase-matched seams; holds/slow movements use a useful judged duration. Crops keep the trainer consistently prominent without clipping hands, feet, dumbbells or motion; side/equipment/form/mocap metadata is complete; ffprobe reports zero audio streams; re-runs are idempotent; no media enters Git.
notes: The complete MadFit source video 07c6wlJh89U is already retained privately at /home/oliver/Projects/fittimer-media-research/growing-gap-scout/baseline/07c6wlJh89U/ with its research evidence in growing-gap-scout/REPORT.md and movement-coverage.csv. Reuse it; do not redownload.

title: Fill W1-W4 clip DB gaps from form-focused female YouTube trainers
description:
## Background
After the first MadFit 30-exercise clip pack proves the database format, FitTimer needs reference clips for the movements unique to the four W1-W4 routines. The owner prefers popular female trainers with consistently clear form: Pamela Reif, Caroline Girvan, Heather Robertson, Sydney Cummings Houdyshell, Growingannanas and MadFit, with additional sources only for genuine gaps.

## Technical Approach
Read the stable movement IDs from the implemented W1-W4 routines, subtract coverage already present in the MadFit reference-v1 pack, and build data/media/clip-sources.json for the remaining visual-required movements. Search with yt-dlp metadata, chapters and subtitles before downloading. For each movement record aliases, preferred channel/video URL and ID, exact candidate timestamps, side/equipment variant, viewpoint/framing, form-quality notes, loopability, and a simple localOnly flag. Download research sources only into the private media workspace, never the Git checkout.

Prefer a stable camera, full relevant body/equipment visibility, mechanically clear repetitions and an appropriate load/variant over production aesthetics. An explicit poster/text-only classification is valid for movements where motion adds no useful instruction, but every visual-required movement must have a timed source candidate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The source map covers every W1-W4 movement not already covered by reference-v1.
- Every visual-required movement has at least one exact timed source candidate from a form-appropriate demonstration.
- Side, equipment, framing, form quality and loopability are recorded so clip production is mechanical.
- Duplicate aliases resolve to one stable movementId; no source media is committed.
- Research coverage and remaining deliberate poster/text-only movements are summarized by routine.

## Test Plan
Validate the source-map JSON, stable-ID uniqueness, timestamp ordering and exact W1-W4 coverage with a dependency-free script. Spot-check at least one candidate from each selected channel against the recorded movement and timestamps.

## Considerations
This is a source map, not the download/slicing pipeline and not a legal review. Keep the localOnly flag lightweight and focus on visual usefulness.
acceptance_criteria: Against the implemented v2 movement IDs, every W1-W4 visual-required movement not covered by reference-v1 has a validated exact timed candidate or a deliberate poster/text-only classification. Each record includes aliases, side, equipment, form, loop range/phase, and a proposed normalized 16:9 landscape crop/safe frame so production is mechanical; source media remains private and the retained corpus is searched before any new download.
notes:
Private source research completed 2026-08-10 and retained outside Git under /home/oliver/Projects/fittimer-media-research/ (inventory README at that root).

Evidence:
- caroline-sydney/report.md — 6 videos, 668 MB; strongest exact primitives in Sydney 0EuxVlfxyNE and strength mechanics in Caroline kaNktg56JaI.
- growing-gap-scout/REPORT.md + movement-coverage.csv — 72-row gap matrix; MadFit baseline plus Growingannanas KIcAjq0MuoI, WxAkMuXERBE, R0eqxnSyRkM.
- pamela-heather/report.md — 6 videos, 449 MB; strongest broad source Heather g-i3S1fnQbQ and clear loop schedules across Heather/Pamela.
Total retained: 16 source videos at 1280x720, about 1.5 GB, with metadata/subtitles where available. Keep all of it and search this corpus before downloading more.

Coverage caution: the existing movement-coverage.csv was computed against draft v1. Recompute against the movement IDs implemented from draft-routines-v2.md; v2 removed several v1 movements and added new isometrics/mobility primitives.

title: Private clip production pipeline: yt-dlp + ffmpeg slice/loop/compress
description:
## Background
FitTimer needs one repeatable way to turn private source videos plus timestamp records into short phone-friendly exercise loops. The produced source/clip files are personal local media and must stay outside the public repository.

## Technical Approach
Build dependency-free scripts/media tooling that shells out to installed yt-dlp, ffmpeg and ffprobe. Read clip-source/catalogue records and write H.264 MP4/yuv420p faststart loops plus poster images into a configurable private media directory outside the Git checkout. Cache downloads privately so re-slicing never redownloads a completed source. Strip the audio stream with -an; validate zero audio streams with ffprobe. Preserve full relevant body/equipment framing, use a natural complete repetition or compound sequence, and allow explicit loop trim/crossfade metadata only when needed. Emit pack-manifest records with duration, dimensions, file size and hash. Make repeated runs idempotent.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Two or more sample mappings produce phone-compatible silent loops and posters in the private output directory.
- ffprobe proves zero audio streams; validation rejects missing, audio-bearing, duplicate or unmapped output.
- The second identical run does no download or encode work.
- Source caches and outputs remain outside Git; only reusable scripts/tests are committed.
- Output conforms to the media-pack contract and records deterministic hashes.

## Test Plan
Use tiny synthetic fixtures for command generation, manifest emission and failure cases; run an ffmpeg/ffprobe sample end-to-end and verify Git status contains no media.

## Considerations
Do not hard-code YouTube channels or routine names into the pipeline. Do not write generated clips to data/ or the service-worker shell.
acceptance_criteria: Sample mappings produce idempotent phone-compatible silent 16:9 landscape loops and posters outside Git. Normal movement loops contain roughly 2–5 clean complete reps (normally 5–10 seconds) with matching start/end phases; holds and mobility use an intentionally useful duration. Per-clip crop metadata zooms within a 16:9 frame to a consistent apparent subject scale while preserving hands, feet, equipment and the full motion path; output is scaled without avoidable upsampling. ffprobe proves zero audio streams; hashes/manifests validate; a repeated run performs no download or encode work.

title: MVP: run the MadFit session on the owner's phone (SPEC §7)
description:
Everything needed for the owner to complete one real MadFit 30-min HIIT session on their phone, with their own music playing uninterrupted in the background. - All child beads closed.

title: Routine & block schema + validator; convert MadFit JSON (SPEC §6.1)
description:
The contract everything else depends on — engine, picker, and all future content. Block = named, reusable ordered list of intervals {exerciseId, displayName, gif, workSeconds, restSeconds, side?, coachNote?}. Routine = metadata {title, equipment, estDuration} + ordered list of block refs and/or inline intervals. Must support per-side exercises, combo intervals (two movements alternated in one interval — MadFit #12/#22/#23), and blocks shared across routines. Deliverables: data/SCHEMA.md documenting every field; a dependency-free validator (node scripts/validate.mjs data/routines/*.json); convert data/routines/madfit-30min-hiit.json (interim shape — see its notes field) to the final schema as the reference example.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Validator passes on the converted MadFit routine and rejects committed bad fixtures (missing gif ref, zero/negative seconds, unknown block ref, invalid side) — keep the fixtures in the repo as the validator's test suite.
- Schema expresses per-side exercises, combo intervals, and cross-routine block reuse.
- data/SCHEMA.md documents every field, its optionality, and units.
acceptance_criteria: validator passes on converted MadFit routine and rejects committed bad fixtures; schema covers per-side, combo, and cross-routine block reuse; SCHEMA.md complete
close_reason: Delivered schema v1, reusable block composition, converted 30-interval MadFit routine, dependency-free validator, and fixtures. Verified: validator + fixture tests pass; migration invariants preserve 30:00 duration and all exercise/GIF refs; UBS exits 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Personal settings: cue, voice, and visual preferences
description:
## Background
FitTimer currently has no settings store or settings UI. WebAudio tones are hard-coded, voice is planned but not implemented, and the selected visual pack does not yet exist. This is a one-user personal app, so the goal is a small dependable preference surface rather than an account or profile system.

## Technical Approach
Add a versioned settings module backed by one localStorage key. Validate every load, use stable versioned IDs, and fall back to defaults for missing, malformed, or unknown values without blocking startup. Add a compact home-screen settings panel for:
- cues: pack, enabled, master volume, countdown, halfway;
- voice: pack, enabled, volume, exercise/side/next announcements;
- visuals: selected media-pack ID and reduced motion.
Apply the cue controls to AudioCuePlayer. Persist voice and visual choices for their owning features to consume. Ship one synth cue pack initially; pack selection is an extensibility contract, not a marketplace.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Settings persist across reload and service-worker cache updates.
- Malformed JSON and unknown IDs fall back to documented defaults with no console error or broken workout.
- Cue enable/volume/countdown/halfway controls affect exactly the intended WebAudio events.
- Voice and visual selections are stored as stable IDs and exposed through the settings API.
- The settings panel is usable at 390x844 and does not crowd the workout controls.

## Test Plan
Add dependency-free unit tests for load/save/migration/default fallback and AudioCuePlayer filtering/volume. Run node --test, scripts/check-pwa.mjs, and a 390x844 browser pass covering edit, reload, and corrupt-storage recovery.

## Considerations
Do not store media blobs or workout history in the settings key. Missing packs must degrade safely to built-in defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Versioned cue/voice/visual preferences persist; malformed or unknown settings fail safely; cue enable, volume, countdown, and halfway controls work; 390x844 browser flow and unit tests pass.

title: Media-pack contract: stable movement IDs and pluggable visuals
description:
## Background
Schema v1 binds each movement directly to a data/gifs path, so the exercise meaning and its current rendering cannot vary independently. FitTimer needs stable movement identities that can resolve through the built-in GIFs today and private silent-video packs later.

## Technical Approach
Introduce schemaVersion 2 for movement visuals. Each movement carries a stable movementId plus displayName and optional exerciseId/textOnly semantics. Define a small versioned media-pack manifest mapping movementId to one or more render assets: silent video, animated WebP or GIF, poster, safe-framing metadata, anatomical side, and an explicit mirroring policy. Generate a built-in gif-v1 manifest from the current MadFit mappings and migrate the current block/routine without visual change. Update SCHEMA.md, validator, fixtures, content URL collection, and runtime resolution. A missing pack entry must fall back to poster/text rather than blank UI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All current content validates as schemaVersion 2 and the MadFit workout looks unchanged with gif-v1.
- Validator rejects missing movementId, invalid pack records, and uncovered referenced movement IDs.
- Adding or changing a visual for an existing movement requires only a media-pack data change, not app code or routine changes.
- Offline caching resolves only the selected pack assets referenced by installed routines.
- Framing and mirroring rules are explicit data, not filename or pixel heuristics.

## Test Plan
Add focused validator fixtures for the new failure modes, run scripts/test-validator.mjs, node --test, scripts/check-pwa.mjs, and a browser offline-reload workout using gif-v1.

## Considerations
This is a direct early-project schema migration; do not add v1 compatibility wrappers. Keep the manifest intentionally small and local-first.
acceptance_criteria: Schema v2 separates stable movement IDs from visual files; current MadFit content migrates with unchanged gif-v1 rendering; manifests validate explicit asset type, normalized 16:9 landscape crop/safe-framing, anatomical side and mirroring; changing a visual is data-only; missing entries fall back safely; selected-pack offline resolution and tests pass.
close_reason: Schema v2 media contract delivered in caabb9d plus offline import-closure fix 94386ca. Independent verification: validator fixtures pass; node --test 28/28; PWA static check proves all 4 transitive JS modules precached; all data JSON parses; Playwright/Chrome at 844x390 confirms 16:9 stage, 27 referenced GIFs plus settings module in fittimer-v2, no catalog cache, Step Jacks rendering, and clean offline reload; UBS 0 critical, only lifecycle false-positive warnings.

title: Private clip-pack import, offline storage, and background-music gate
description:
## Background
Basic video-card rendering does not by itself let the public Pages app use personal source clips. This feature imports one private pack onto the owner's device, stores it offline and selects it without publishing its media.

## Technical Approach
Add a local pack-import flow for a manifest plus files produced by the clip pipeline. Validate the manifest contract, store media blobs and manifest metadata in browser storage suitable for offline playback, and keep only the selected pack ID in settings. Feed stored responses/blob URLs into the existing video renderer. Support one selected private pack plus the built-in gif-v1 fallback. Packs survive reload and airplane mode and can be removed. Unknown, corrupt or missing versions fall back cleanly. No private file becomes a service-worker precache URL served from Pages.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The completed MadFit reference-v1 pack imports on the target phone, survives reload, and runs in airplane mode.
- Removing, corrupting or selecting an unknown pack falls back to built-in media without blank UI.
- Reduced motion uses posters and no autoplaying clips.
- With background music playing, a full video-bearing workout does not pause or duck music on the owner's target Android and iOS browsers; this evidence is required to close.
- No private media appears in Git history, Git status or the public Pages asset list.

## Test Plan
Unit-test import validation/storage/fallback, run a desktop import/offline browser pass, then record full real-phone Android/iOS background-music evidence using reference-v1.

## Considerations
No pack marketplace, sharing, accounts or remote sync.
acceptance_criteria: Both reference-v1 and w1w4-v1 import on the target phone, survive reload, and run in airplane mode with every W1-W4 visual-required movement resolving through the documented fallback chain. Missing/corrupt packs fall back without blank UI; reduced motion uses posters; a full video-bearing workout on target Android and iOS does not pause or duck background music; no private media enters Git or public Pages assets.

title: Workout-stage video renderer with image/poster/text fallback
description:
## Background
The workout stage currently renders images or text. Media-pack entries need a bounded video-card renderer before private pack import/storage is added.

## Technical Approach
Resolve the current movement through the media-pack API and render a video entry with muted, autoplay, loop and playsInline set as DOM properties, poster fallback, no controls, no audio element and no Media Session. Fall back through animated WebP/GIF, poster and text. Honor explicit framing/mirroring metadata and object containment. Only mount the current and optional next clip; release obsolete blob URLs/elements during interval changes. Re-play an already selected clip after visibility restoration when allowed. Reduced-motion selection remains owned by settings/media resolution and must yield a poster rather than autoplay.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A synthetic mixed-media routine renders video, image, poster and text entries through the documented fallback chain.
- Video elements are muted/playsInline/looping, remain safely framed, and are removed as intervals advance without accumulation.
- Missing or failed video playback falls back without a blank stage.
- Static checks preserve the no-audio-element/no-Media-Session invariant.
- Automated browser checks pass at phone viewport and after visibility restoration.

## Test Plan
Unit-test media selection and fallback as pure logic, extend PWA static checks, and run a phone-sized desktop browser pass with a tiny synthetic no-audio video.

## Considerations
This bead does not import private packs, persist media offline, or claim real-phone music coexistence; ft-mvp-ow6.15 owns those risks.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic mixed-media routine renders a bounded landscape-first 16:9 stage with muted playsInline video and image/poster/text fallbacks; explicit crop/framing is honored without clipping motion; no element accumulation, audio element or Media Session; automated browser/PWA checks pass at 844x390 landscape and portrait fallback after visibility restoration.

title: PWA shell: offline via service worker, installable (SPEC §6.2)
description: Implement the installable offline PWA shell: index.html, manifest, and service worker with correct GitHub Pages scope. Precache the app shell and only media referenced by installed routines; cache discovered routine/block/media URLs without precaching the full exercise catalog. This bead owns the implementation and automated browser proof. Real Android/iOS Add-to-Home-Screen and a full airplane-mode phone session are retained in ft-mvp-ow6.11.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest and service-worker scopes are valid; the app shell plus installed routine assets load after an online visit; a 390x844 Chromium online-to-offline reload can select and start a routine; cache-version changes pick up changed content; static checks reject broad catalog precaching.
notes: GitHub Pages production smoke test passed at https://odcpw.github.io/fittimer/ on 2026-08-10: fresh Chromium 390x844 loaded the routine, registered/cached the service worker, started interval 1/30, then reloaded offline and started again with zero page/console errors. Remaining acceptance: Android and iOS Add-to-Home-Screen plus a complete real-device airplane-mode session.
close_reason: Implementation complete and automated offline behavior verified: node --test, validator fixtures, check-pwa, and prior production Chromium 390x844 online/offline reload+start pass. Real-device A2HS/airplane evidence remains explicitly gated by ft-mvp-ow6.11.

title: Interval engine: timestamp-anchored state machine (SPEC §6.3)
description:
Pure JS state machine (idle/work/rest/paused/done) as a standalone module with no DOM access (SPEC §6.3). Timing is timestamp-anchored: compute remaining time from clock deltas, never accumulate setInterval ticks. Controls: pause/resume, skip forward/back one interval, restart. Emits tick, intervalStart, intervalEnd, halfway, countdown321; UI and audio are subscribers only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests (node --test, injected fake clock, zero deps) cover: every state transition, pause/resume across a work→rest boundary, skip at first/last interval, restart, and recovery after a simulated 10s stall.
- A 30-interval run finishes within 1s of wall clock.
- Skip/pause/resume never desync display state from engine state.
acceptance_criteria: node --test suite passes (fake clock: transitions, boundary pause/resume, edge skips, 10s stall); 30-interval run within 1s of wall clock
close_reason: Delivered pure timestamp-anchored idle/work/rest/paused/done engine with pause/resume, skip both directions, restart, and required events. node --test passes fake-clock transitions, boundary pause/resume, edge skips, restart, 10s stall recovery, cue timing, and 30-minute wall-clock anchoring; UBS exits 0 after triage.

title: Workout screen UI + navigation: Previous / End Workout / completion (SPEC §6.4)
description:
## Background
The phone-first workout screen is implemented and its GIF cropping defect is fixed. Navigation semantics remain confusing: Back calls engine.skipBack(), silently does nothing during interval 1, and changes meaning to Home only after completion. There is no deliberate way to end an active workout.

## Technical Approach
Preserve the existing timer engine. Rename Back to Previous and visibly disable it throughout interval 1. Add an explicit End Workout control that pauses and opens an in-app confirmation; Keep Going resumes from the paused timestamp, while End returns home and stops the animation loop. On completion, show explicit Home and Restart actions rather than repurposing unrelated controls. Keep Previous/Next/Pause sized and placed for sweaty-thumb use. Retain the next-up rest preview, text-only fallback, safe media containment, progress, and responsive dark layout.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Previous is visibly disabled during interval 1 work/rest and works from interval 2 onward.
- End Workout always requires confirmation; cancelling resumes accurately and confirming returns home with no running timer/animation.
- Completion presents explicit Home and Restart actions and both work.
- The existing rest preview, text-only interval, safe framing and full-session phone ergonomics remain correct.
- A 390x844 browser flow and the eventual real-phone workout reveal no navigation mis-taps.

## Test Plan
Extend the browser/E2E pass for interval-1 disabled state, Previous from interval 2, End/cancel/confirm, Home and Restart after completion. Run node --test and scripts/check-pwa.mjs.

## Considerations
Do not overload Home as an active-workout skip. History/partial-completion recording remains owned by ft-mvp-ow6.12.
acceptance_criteria: Previous is disabled at interval 1 and functional later; confirmed End returns home and cancel resumes accurately; completion has working Home/Restart; installed PWA declares landscape orientation; controls and a true 16:9 safely framed stage pass an 844x390 landscape-first workout flow with portrait fallback and no navigation mis-taps.
notes: Workout UI is implemented. GIF clipping defect found during visual QA: intrinsic square grid items rendered 348px tall inside a 254px stage despite object-fit: contain. Fixed by constraining the grid row with minmax(0, 1fr) and allowing image min-height: 0. Playwright at 390x844 and 1024x900 confirms complete single and two-GIF interval renders with zero page/console errors. Bead remains open pending a full real-phone session/mis-tap check.
close_reason: Delivered af4c8b5: explicit Previous/End/Home/Restart semantics, landscape manifest and true 16:9 stage. Verified node --check, 30 focused tests, scripts/check-pwa.mjs, and real Chrome flows at 844x390 and 390x844 with accurate pause/resume, end confirm/cancel, completion actions, >=44px controls, no horizontal overflow, and zero console/page errors. Real-device full workout remains ft-mvp-ow6.11.

title: Audio cues via WebAudio that don't kill background music (SPEC §6.5)
description: Implement synthesized WebAudio cues for countdown, work start, rest start, and optional halfway events. Create/resume one AudioContext from the Start gesture and suppress stale catch-up cues. Never create an audio element or Media Session. This bead owns the cue implementation and automated proof. Real Android/iOS background-music coexistence is retained in ft-mvp-ow6.11 and the private-video gate in ft-mvp-ow6.15.
acceptance_criteria: All intended engine cue events produce distinct tested tone profiles; Start unlocks/resumes one WebAudio context; stale/unrelated events stay silent; dispose closes the context; static checks prove no audio element or Media Session use.
notes: Implemented WebAudio-only synthesized cues for intervalStart, intervalEnd, halfway, and countdown321. AudioContext is created/resumed from the Start gesture; stale catch-up events are suppressed. Verified with 5 unit tests, full 15-test suite, PWA policy checks forbidding <audio>/Media Session, and a real Chromium browser unlock/start check at 390x844 with no page errors. Acceptance remains open pending Spotify mixing verification on real Android Chrome and iOS Safari through a full session.
close_reason: WebAudio-only cue implementation is complete. Fresh baseline: node --test passed 15/15 including 5 audio tests; scripts/check-pwa.mjs passed the no-audio-element/no-Media-Session policy. Real-device music coexistence remains in ft-mvp-ow6.11 and ft-mvp-ow6.15.

title: Voice: pre-rendered FrankenTTS clips + SpeechSynthesis fallback (SPEC §6.6)
description: Pre-render the finite phrase vocabulary for every installed routine with FrankenTTS at content-build time on the 3090, then play clips through WebAudio. The routine-driven render tool covers movement names, sides, go/rest, and digits for MadFit plus W1-W4. Use SpeechSynthesis only for a missing phrase after Start-gesture unlock. Consume ft-mvp-ow6.13 voice settings, announce the next exercise during rest, and queue speech so it never overlaps countdown cues.
acceptance_criteria: MadFit and all W1-W4 movement/side/boundary phrases have pre-rendered clips; a deliberately missing phrase uses SpeechSynthesis after Start unlock; enabled/pack/volume/announcement settings apply; speech never overlaps countdown cues; an accelerated eyes-free browser run covers every installed routine.
notes: Consume voice pack/enabled/volume/announcement preferences from ft-mvp-ow6.13; do not create a second settings store or UI.

title: Wake lock + ergonomics (SPEC §6.7)
description:
Screen Wake Lock API with re-acquire on visibilitychange (SPEC §6.7; iOS needs >= 16.4). The engine's timestamp anchoring must keep the timer honest through brief backgrounding — verify on-device, don't assume.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Screen stays on through a full 30-min session on the owner's phone.
- Backgrounding the tab for 10s and returning shows correct remaining time and interval, and the wake lock is re-acquired.
acceptance_criteria: screen stays on for a full 30-min session; 10s backgrounding preserves correct time/interval and re-acquires the lock

title: Home screen routine picker, zero-code routine add (SPEC §6.8)
description:
Home screen lists routines from data/routines/ with title, duration, equipment, exercise count; tap to start (SPEC §6.8). Static hosting has no directory listing, so the picker needs a precached routine index as DATA (e.g. data/routines/index.json, kept by the ft-mvp-ow6.1 validator or by hand per SCHEMA.md) — dropping in a routine file must never require touching app code. Leave a layout slot for history/streaks (ft-mvp-ow6.12); do not build it yet.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Adding a routine JSON (+ its index entry) makes it appear and run with zero app-code changes.
- Displayed metadata matches the routine file's contents.
acceptance_criteria: new routine JSON + index entry appears and runs with zero app-code changes; displayed metadata matches file
